newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Asian carriers increase Benelux capacity.
newsitem.headline: Asian carriers increase Benelux capacity.

text.p: Asian carriers are increasing capacity in the Benelux market, following a surge in demand.
Air Hong Kong will be increasing its frequencies ex-Brussels from May 5, said the carrier's European general manager, Marcel Buelens.

The Hong Kong carrier, daughter company of Cathay Pacific, will up its 747-200 freighter flights from four to five a week. Then soon after the carrier is hoping to increase this to six flights a week, he added.
This move follows AHK's withdrawal of capacity in the early part of the year. "In the first two weeks of January it was a struggle to fill the capacity so we withdrew two frequencies."
"We attempted to stabilise the market as rates were under pressure but from mid-February it has been very busy and we have had to turn away business," he added.
In March, the carrier has had an average load factor of around 90 percent. "It is a less aggressive market rate-wise to Hong Kong" he said.

EVA Air is another Asian carrier increasing its Benelux-Asia capacity as it has decided to transfer part of its freighter service from Schiphol to Brussels Airport, Hans Lin, EVA European general manager, told Reuters.
Taiwan's EVA, will start a twice-weekly freighter service into Brussels on May 10. Meanwhile, the airline will still have a weekly freighter service into Schiphol, he said.
The carrier operates a three-times-a-week freighter service into the Dutch airport with an MD-11 freighter.
As well as moving the two freighter services, the Taiwanese carrier will begin an MD-11 passenger service into Amsterdam, on a three-times-a-week basis from May 9.
"We will now have six flights a week into the Benelux to offer shippers," he added.

Korean Airlines also added a second freighter into the Amsterdam market last week. The Seoul carrier introduced a 747- 200 freighter last week which adds to a 747-400F the carrier already flies between Amsterdam and Seoul.
